Landon Tresp, 16, left, met the girl playing Among Us before alerting his mother, Khristina, 41, to the missing teen's predicament.

Sixteen-year-old Landon Tresp was in the bedroom of his family's Colorado mountain home, playing an online game after finishing his daily chores, when he began chatting on his laptop with another player.

She was also a teenager, and the pair "kind of just clicked," he tells the BBC.

In a recent development, he told her he liked her name, and she confessed that it was an alias. She was a runaway, she said - and was being held against her will, hundreds of miles from home, though she didn't know exactly where. The girl, 17, and had been missing for more than a year.

In a recent development, stunned, Landon felt "helpless," he claims - and, after learning more details over two weeks of chatting, he decided to tell his mother, Khristina on 31 October this year. The 41-year-old nurse and mother of five was putting Halloween makeup on her younger children for trick-or-treating when he briefed her.

That set the mother and son on a path to track down his friend, contact her mother, cooperate with the FBI - and ultimately witness the rescue of the teen - only 24 hours after Landon first alerted Khristina to her plight.

"She had one opportunity to reach out her hand and ask for help, and she chose me," Khristina states of the girl, who was 15 when she went missing.

A screenshot shows Khristina on a call with the girl as she highlighted her the knife her alleged captor kept under his pillow.

The Tresps have shared with BBC screenshots of communication with the girl and a photo matching the criminal complaint to corroborate their story.

Landon first told his mother about "Jenny" - whose identity the BBC is protecting - in mid-October, a few weeks before the rescue.

"He had mentioned something about maybe a week or so into talking to her that he met a girl online, and she was really sweet," says Khristina - who cautioned him that "you don't always know who's on the other side of the screen".

"She's just having a really hard time and looking for a friend," he told her.

But Landon was becoming increasingly concerned as Jenny told him more about her situation.

They'd met playing Among Us, a game Landon describes as "kind of like online space Clue".

After telling Landon that she was a runaway, "Jenny" noted an older man had taken her across state lines and wouldn't let her leave. She was the subject of a missing person investigation, and she sent Landon links to stories about her disappearance. But she believed police were no longer looking for her.

Jenny was scared and desperate, and that's why Landon went to his mother.

Her maternal instincts on high alert, Khristina contacted Jenny herself on Discord, the encrypted platform.

During the conversation, Khristina mentioned she told the Colorado mother how she'd been through "years of abuse in her life and lots and lots of problems".

Within hours, Jenny started calling Khristina "mama".

Among Us supports cross platform play online with 4-15 players on various devices.

In a recent development, the Colorado mother knew things were serious when she read the missing persons articles. Jenny knew she was in Oregon and gave the name of a city, but she didn't know where she was being held exactly. Khristina knew she needed more. She told Jenny to find a piece of mail or another document in the house that had a full name on it, which the girl did.

"That's when I went to work," Khristina claims, delving into tax and property records.

Industry observers note that khristina narrowed down addresses, then searched them on a real estate site to find pictures. She showed the photos to Jenny, who confirmed that the second one was where she was being held.

The "next thing she asked me was to please not tell anyone until [her captor] was gone - that he did have weapons in the house and she was very scared," Khristina remarked.

According to recent reports, jenny promised Khristina she'd call her back through the game platform when he left the next morning, and in the meantime Khristina began looking for the law enforcement agency that had been assigned to the missing teen's case. She contacted Jenny's mother on social media, spoke briefly to her on the phone and then got a call from an FBI agent.

"Have you seen her alive?'" the agent asked Khristina.

"And I remarked: 'I have; I video chatted with her, I've seen her, and she goes 'Oh my God, I cannot believe any of this'," Khristina recalled.

When Jenny called Khristina back after her alleged captor left home, the FBI monitored their conversation. According to the criminal complaint's record of the conversation, Jenny explained how she'd met Adam Hunter Harmel on social media in May 2025.

He'd told her he was disabled and his hips were "messed up," offering Jenny money if she'd help get him to Oregon.

It has been revealed that after he picked her up in Utah, however, Harmel threw her phone into a river, drove her to Oregon and kept her in the basement. He forced her to sleep against the wall in his bed, with a knife under his pillow, to prevent her from escaping. He gave Jenny a cell phone with no ability to make calls, but it could connect to wifi, which is how she played the online game.

The 39-year-old "would become violent and aggressive", the document says, which included hitting her and sexually assaulting her.

He also allegedly forced Jenny to remove her braces with pliers so she wouldn't be identifiable.

As Khristina and the FBI heard all of this, law enforcement were staging to bring Jenny to safety, after being alerted to her whereabouts.

While Harmel was out of the home, officers were sent to the street and the address, and Khristina was prepping Jenny for her run to freedom.

She'd unsuccessfully tried escaping before, she told Khristina.

Law enforcement was "phenomenalâ¦giving me an revision, you know, 'We're nine minutes out, we're seven minutes out,'" says Khristina, who was on the phone with Jenny the entire time, her son Landon watching at her side.

Khristina could hear other people in the home with Jenny, and she was afraid that someone would catch wind of what was happening and harm the girl.

But she kept any of those fears from Jenny.

Recent findings suggest that "I want you to take three deep breaths with me," she told the teen. "When an officer tells me to go, and I relay that message to you, I want you to run up those stairs as fast as you can â¦ Grab that basement door.

"I want you to keep going down that hallway and grab that front doorâ¦ do not stop.'".

The mother and son watched breathlessly as Jenny ran into the arms of a state trooper.

Harmel is now in federal custody and has been charged in a criminal complaint with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity. Local Oregon media also reported he'd been accused of sexually abusing a six-year-old in the months before Jenny disappeared - and a sexual abuse protective order was granted against him in March 2025.

He remains behind bars awaiting trial.

A lawyer for the defendant did not respond to a BBC request for comment.

Jenny, meanwhile, remains in daily communication with Khristina and Landon - who still enjoys playing online games with her.

"Sometimes we just sit on video chat, just so she knows she has someone that cares," Khristina notes. "She was on video last night when I cooked dinner â¦it's nice to know that when she has a bad day or a bad moment, she can call me right away or call Landon right away.".

"She's doing great for what she's gone through.".

They haven't met in person yet, but they're in the process of trying to make that happen.

"I hope I can put my arms around her soon," Khristina says.

#58890. Europe is entering a ‘supercycle’ of national elections. Their outcomes could shake the EU’s foundations

Europe is entering a ‘supercycle’ of national elections. Their outcomes could shake the EU’s foundations

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1274 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As nationalist, Eurosceptic parties surge in four of the bloc’s biggest member states, the coming year’s polls could test its resilience like never before.
  • Sources indicate that in late 1998, Tony Blair was prime minister of Britain, Lionel Jospin was prime minister of France, and Gerhard Schröder had just been elected chancellor of Germany.
  • Brisk economic growth was lifting living standards.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As nationalist, Eurosceptic parties surge in four of the bloc’s biggest member states, the coming year’s polls could test its resilience like never before.

Sources indicate that in late 1998, Tony Blair was prime minister of Britain, Lionel Jospin was prime minister of France, and Gerhard Schröder had just been elected chancellor of Germany. The EU had 15 member states and pro-European, centre-left parties were in power – either alone or in coalitions – in all but two of them.

Brisk economic growth was lifting living standards. Eastward enlargement was under way. In Washington, Bill Clinton was pursuing the same brand of “third way” centrism as a middle path between free-market capitalism and traditional socialism. The EU felt like it had the tide of history behind it.

Not quite three decades later, the continent’s politics once again seem to be tilting in a single direction – except this time, the momentum belongs to the nationalist far right, and the outcome could be a significant unpicking of the postwar European consensus that built the EU.

According to recent reports, between the end of this month and the end of next year, an extraordinary electoral sequence will sweep the bloc. Voters in four of the EU’s five biggest member states, by population and economy, head to the polls, with parliamentary elections also due in Estonia, Finland, Greece and Slovakia, and regional ballots in Germany.

Spain kicks off the cycle with a snap general election on 29 November, with prime minister Pedro Sánchez’s socialist coalition facing probable defeat to rightwing parties in the shape of the conservative People’s party (PP) and far-right Vox, which already govern together in some Spanish regions.

Next come presidential and parliamentary elections in France in the spring. The clear frontrunner in the presidential race is Marine Le Pen of far-right the National Rally (RN), well ahead of the far-left firebrand Jean-Luc Mélenchon and a hopelessly divided mainstream opposition.

When Poland votes later next year, nationalist parties that between them command nearly half the national vote could well unseat the liberal coalition of prime minister, Donald Tusk, despite recent splits. And in Italy, Giorgia Meloni, whose Brothers of Italy party has far-right roots, hopes to secure a second term in elections due before the end of 2027 – while facing pressure on her right flank from the upstart National Future party.

Paradoxically, this nationalist surge arrives amid strong public support for the EU. Shocked by the chaos of Brexit and seeking reassurance in an increasingly alarming world, a record 74% of Europeans say their country benefits from membership, and very few Eurosceptic parties now advocate leaving outright.

Industry observers note that the Eurosceptics and nationalists do, however, still view the bloc as a top-down project that undermines national sovereignty, and aim to transform it into an altogether looser association of sovereign nation-states. In the words of the Italian political scientist Natalie Tocci, that means this coming electoral supercycle could “dramatically change the face of Europe” – triggering not simply “a slow erosion of the European project but a hollowing out, if not an outright implosion”.

All elections differ and national specifics loom large. But analysts agree the underlying forces at work here are connected: sluggish growth, ageing populations, strained public finances and a spiralling cost of living have chipped away at support for Europe’s traditional catch-all centre-left and centre-right parties. The wave of youth-led protests sweeping Europe is only the most visible sign of deep voter discontent.

Meanwhile, nationalist parties have become increasingly adept at conjuring and exploiting an ever-evolving list of supposed threats and crises, from migration and vaccines to the green transition, support for Ukraine, globalisation, international elites and supranational institutions – narratives bolstered by Russian disinformation and overt backing for “patriotic” parties from Donald Trump’s White House. As a result, politics has fragmented, and polarised: nearly one in four voters now backs far-right parties – a share that has grown almost fivefold since the mid-1990s.

The rise has not been linear: over the past year or so, while the far-right Alternative für Deutschland scored a historic regional election victory in eastern Germany, in the Netherlands Geert Wilders’s Freedom party lost nearly a third of its seats, Viktor Orbán’s Fidesz was soundly beaten in Hungary and the far-right Sweden Democrats shed support for the first time in 16 years.

But the underlying upward trend appears clear – fuelled above all, political scientists argue, by the normalisation and mainstreaming of far-right ideas, most notably on immigration. Centre-right parties are gradually dismantling “firewalls” that once barred cooperation with the radical right. At the European level, the centre-right European People’s party has increasingly turned to farther-right groups to roll back parts of the European green deal and tighten migration rules.

According to recent reports, for the EU, the biggest impact of this election supercycle could be in the European Council of national leaders, which now features just three centre-left heads of government out of 27. If Eurosceptic leaders in France, Spain and Poland join those of Czechia, Italy, Romania, Slovakia and Slovenia by the end of 2027, they would not have the numbers to rewrite EU law – but they would constitute a formidable blocking minority.

EU budget negotiations, future enlargement, aid to Ukraine and deeper integration in essential fields such as defence, energy, finance and technology could all face paralysis, analysts warn.

Safety in numbers, notes Tocci, could change current leaders’ behaviour in the council. Meloni’s relative restraint has been dictated, in part, by her relative isolation among mainstream peers such as Tusk, Sánchez and France’s Emmanuel Macron (alongside Rome’s reliance on €200bn in EU recovery funds).

If she were instead sitting down with the likes of Le Pen, Poland’s far-right Law and Justice (PiS) leader, Jarosław Kaczyński, and a Vox-backed Spanish government, with National Future’s hardline Roberto Vannacci breathing down her neck at home and those EU funds winding down, she might have less incentive to play pro-EU ball.

Industry observers note that analysts agree, though, that the decisive battleground is France. Le Pen’s election platform sets her on a collision course with Brussels: she aims to cut €11bn from France’s EU budget contribution, hold a constitutional referendum to proclaim the supremacy of French over European law, and breach various single-market rules.

According to recent reports, and France “carries very significant influence over the EU”, stated Mujtaba Rahman of the Eurasia Group consultancy. Compared with Orbán, he notes, a president Le Pen would have “far more leverage to carry out the far-right playbook of subverting the EU’s law-based, supranational architecture”.

Recent findings suggest that until now, Brussels has contained disruptors such as Orbán largely because there were rarely more than two or three round the table. A cohesive Eurosceptic bloc would leave the EU unable to enforce rule-of-law standards, further integrate economic and security policies or, indeed, agree on anything much at all. The first victim would very probably be Ukraine, with Le Pen leading a blocking caucus against further aid.

Industry observers note that three decades on from 1998, Europe’s coming elections, concluded Stefan Lehne of the Carnegie Europe thinktank, could well turn into “key tests of the EU’s resilience”. The threat to the bloc might not be immediate or existential, he stated, but the medium-term risks were significant.

“A stronger role for the radical right may be unlikely to dismantle the EU as it exists today,” Lehne remarked, but could “prevent it from becoming what it needs to be to deal with the challenges of the future”. And gradually but inevitably, prolonged failure to act collectively as and where needed would lead a “loss of relevance”.

Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.
  • It has been revealed that the balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source noted, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it.
  • Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

It has been revealed that the balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source noted, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical fresh insights to the People’s Republic of China.”.

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it indicates is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the latest intelligence.

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”.

Industry observers note that gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”.

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

In a recent development, still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

CNN’s Alex Marquardt contributed to this report.

Plus, there are a handful of side pockets inside, but none are large enough for my massive Owala water bottle. I have the 30L in Butter, but there's also a smaller 20L version if you're looking for something a little more compact.

If your mom wants something a little more stylish, the Alex Mill totes are always on my mind. They come in a variety of gorgeous colors and are made of coated canvas, so they can put up with daily adventures, and you can customize them with your mom's initials (or even just the word “mom”!) with Alex Mill's hand-painted letter service. It's a simpler tote with no other pockets, but you can use the top snaps to let out the sides or tuck them in, depending on how much space Mom needs on a given day. The weathered color and vibe of these bags also feel perfect for the fall season.

My latest favorite family planning gadget is a digital wall calendar. These handy devices take the Google Calendar I live by (and just about any other digital calendar, if your mom isn't a Google girl) and put it on a physical device I can rapidly tap into without needing to grab my phone or bark at Alexa. The Skylight Calendar 2 is my favorite, because it not only includes to-do lists, meal planning, and a recipe book but also doubles as a digital photo frame. That means it displays cute photos of my family most of the time, and then, with a simple tap, it opens the calendar or whatever page I was last on to show me what's on my family's schedule. It does have a subscription fee, though, to get the digital photo frame feature and a few other options, like meal planning. But I think it's well worth it to get so many features in a single device. You can also gift her kiddo a Skylight Buddy ($140) so that she doesn't have to remind them to check the main calendar for their chores; it'll appear on their own device if they have a Buddy.

To me, motherhood is all about change. It's most obvious at the start of motherhood, when your body changes a lot over the course of nine months, but motherhood encompasses the rest of our lives, and our bodies and style change a lot over that time. One of the biggest giveaways that time has gone by is our clothes—how well they fit for our current stage, whether they reflect the time of our life right now, and if we're bored out of our skull with everything but don't want to buy an entirely latest closet.

I've been loving renting from Nuuly this pregnancy because the brand has an entire maternity section that lets me find pieces to fit me in this short—but very different size—season of my life. My older mother also loves having a clothing subscription because she gets bored of her outfit options to wear into the office, and I loved it for the same reason when I had my first clothing subscription right out of college. If Mom has been talking about wanting some newly introduced looks but feels overwhelmed about what she wants to invest in, these rental services are a fun way to get a lot of new clothes in your life without having to store them or spend as much as you would have (some of my favorite maternity clothes I've gotten through Nuuly would have cost me $200 apiece!) The service costs $98 a month, but your first month is discounted to just $60. There's one piece I miss already that might drive me to pick up a second subscription, which would genuinely be cheaper than buying the piece I want brand new.

For years, the go-to gift for a woman in my family, mother or not, was shopping in the jewelry section of a department store. My mom even helped orchestrate this for the rest of the aunties and grandmas, but now, as a mom myself, I find myself interested in jewelry that tells a story about my family and children instead of just any old set. (Except extra earrings for my earring stack, a gift I'm thrilled to get, because there's never enough.).

It has been revealed that I love these pieces from Gorjana and BaubleBar that you can customize. Gorjana has a ton of charms you can add to its necklaces or bracelets to reflect Mom’s kids’ initials, birthstones, or anything else; I paired a charm of my son’s first initial ($50) with the Wilshire Adjustable Necklace ($68). If she's more of a ring gal, BaubleBar's Toi et Moi ring ($78) lets you choose two birthstones to display. I chose my and my son's birthstones, but luckily his sibling-to-be will also have a red birthstone, so it'll remain a perfect reflection of my kids and me for years to come.

This item was literally made for sports moms: a padded stadium cushion with a wearable blanket inside. My son plays on three sports teams, so I do a lot of sitting outside on bleachers and turf sidelines—and often at night, when it’s freezing. I’ve tried many things to keep warm, from heated jackets to HotHands, but nothing has worked as well as this water-resistant blanket, which unfurls to 50 x 70 inches and sports a clip at the front so you can wear it like a cape. It can also be used for picnics or as a spot for younger siblings to sit and read during tournaments. It’s also not hard to fold it back up and fit it inside the seat part (which is 1 inch thick without the blanket inside). It comes in six colors, so you can be sure to find one that matches your giftee’s kid’s team or school colors. —Kat Merck.

As a mom, I take a lot of photos of my family. A lot. And sometimes it feels like all those great photos of my son's milestones go to my camera roll and photo storage to die. There are two solutions I love for this that are incredibly giftable: a digital photo frame she can instantly upload images to, and a printed photo book where you can take the best of the best and put them at her fingertips. I have and love both for different reasons.

I love the digital photo frame to add all the photos from a fun weekend at the San Diego Zoo or Renaissance Pleasure Faire for me to relive again and again, but I also love being able to pull a photo book from the bookshelf and relive a specific moment I know is waiting there for me. Aura makes my favorite digital photo frames (followed by Skylight's Calendar 2 if you want a multipurpose device, but Aura has no subscription fee if you only want photos), while Mixbook has been a favorite of mine for a while when it comes to printing photos, and has great starting prices for its photo books.

According to recent reports, the graduation from diaper-bag-carrying mom to tote-full-of-snacks-and-clothes-changes mom to an adult who only needs to carry their own stuff is a parenting milestone that deserves celebration. This is my favorite grown-up mom bag, which holds only the essentials: water (because no matter how old your kids are, someone is going to get thirsty), cards, phone, and keys. The thick strap makes it comfortable to carry, and there’s a color, material, or theme for just about anyone’s vibe, including a fresh line of clear stadium versions. All WanderFull bags will hold any handle-less water bottle up to 11 inches tall and 3.5 inches in diameter. —Kat Merck.

Recent findings suggest that once my kiddo is asleep, you can find me parked on the couch playing video games. I upgraded to a Nintendo Switch 2 ($499) earlier this summer so I could finally buy and play Pokopia ($70), since it's exclusive to the new console, and now my husband and I are completely hooked on the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time ($60) remake that came out a few weeks ago. It's also swiftly become an experience I can share with my son now that he's 4; he was been helping me and my husband replay Tears of the Kingdom, but now he's dubbed Ocarina of Time as “Major Little Link” and is obsessed with using the grappling hook and using up all of our arrows.

If you're not looking to upgrade her console just yet but need a Switch-friendly cozy game for her, Stardew Valley has another big update in the works and only costs $15. I'm also hoping we see Fields of Mistria ($14) come to the Switch eventually, but the full launch came out in August for Steam users and has major quality-of-life improvements if she has played Stardew one time too many. My husband also upgraded his gaming setup this summer with a Steam Machine (from $1,049), and I have big intends to start using it often for Fields of Mistria. If your mom loves games, she'll love any one of these latest devices or new games, especially if she already got herself the new gadget as I did.

If a mom in your life is exploring her nonalcoholic drink options, The Zero Proof has some gift sets perfect to give so she can try out several things at once. I'm at the moment grounded from drinking any cocktails while I'm pregnant, but moms (and people in general) can have all kinds of reasons to want to explore unique, interesting drinks that are sans alcohol. I really liked this set for how many cool drinks it exposed me to, from bottles of nonalcoholic wine to knockoff cocktails. If you're looking to spend a little less, my favorites so far have been the Château del Ish Non-Alcoholic Sparkling Espumante ($20) and Lapo's Non-Alcoholic Melograno Mule ($20 for four).

Look, I love a Kindle, but if you want to get the best e-reader for your buck (or maybe she just wants an e-reader that isn't a Kindle), the answer is actually a Kobo. My favorite is the Kobo Libra Colour. It's cheaper than the Kindle Colorsoft and can also double as a digital notebook if you add on the $70 stylus. I also prefer Kobo's annotating options: You can write right on the pages instead of in weird pop-up margins and boxes only on Kindle. Kobo also has a page-turner remote ($34), which I love to pair with a pillow stand holder so I can lean back and relax without holding up my e-reader while I read. I gave a similar pillow stand to my mom, and now I can spot her last reading spot easily because that pillow is resting there.

You could also gift her one of the new Kindles if she's a Kindle addict. Many of my friends are drooling over the new purple Ube color of the 12th-gen Kindle ($150), but my personal favorite is the Kindle Aluminum (I just wish it were cheaper!). There's also finally Kindle page-turn remote, the Kindle Click ($35).

According to recent reports, if the mom you know is into LED red-light therapy, she probably already knows about face masks and hair growth devices like the one we recommend above, but there’s one area she’s probably neglecting: her hands. With aging comes loss of collagen, subcutaneous fat, and cumulative effects of UV exposure. I spent the first 26 years of my life living in California, where I rarely remembered to put sunscreen on the tops of my hands. Twenty years later, it reveals—they’re wrinkly and have age spots and look like they belong to someone 15 years my senior. Trust me; no mom wants this. I’ve been using Omnilux’s FDA-cleared red-light glove for the past few months to try to mitigate some of the damage, and while I haven’t seen any changes yet (Omnilux says changes happen in four to six weeks, but in my experience with red-light masks, it typically takes much longer to see results), I very much enjoy using this device on its own. The soft silicone glove is comfortable to wear and warms as it heats up, so it feels good and works to reduce joint pain. It’s easy to do while I’m reading or watching TV—just three 10-minute sessions per week—and the rechargeable battery (USB-C) lasts a little over a week. If your giftee already spends 10 minutes at the end of the day relaxing in an LED face mask, she’ll know exactly what to do here. —Kat Merck.

In a recent development, if you know a mom who loves to bird-watch (I know one!), you can upgrade her bird feeder to a smart one. Smart bird feeders add a camera to the feeder so she can see a close-up feed of the birds that come to hang out in her yard, and they're adorable to boot, for a little smart curb appeal. WIRED reviewer Kat Merck recommends the original Birdfy feeder as a great gift; it's her favorite smart bird feeder and comes in adorable colors to brighten your mom's yard and catch the eye of neighborhood birds. But the one she and I both have our eye on (her for her mother, me for myself) is the Birdfy Nest Duo, which is actually a birdhouse with two cameras so you can see the birds entering the nest outside and raising a family inside.

Sources indicate that I love a backpack when I'm on the move with my 4-year-old, but one thing that annoys me is that things are hard to find inside, because packs are typically so deep. That's why I adore the Mina Baie Emmy Diaper Bag: It's a wide, shallow bag instead of a long one, making it easy to open and see most of what I store in it without digging around. I'm not toting diapers at the moment, but I've used it to pack a ton of snacks, toys, and spare clothing for my kid.

It has been revealed that I'm intrigued to see how using it with two kids goes—I chose the Emmy Midi, which is the midsize bag, but if you're a pumping parent or need to carry a ton of bottles with formula, you might want to try the larger Emmy Full. The stylish bag is made of vegan leather and can be converted from crossbody to tote to backpack mode, depending on which straps you use. Mina Baie doesn't include a changing kit, but sells one separately ($59) if you'd like to include it in your gift (or buy that as the gift to upgrade their existing bag of choice).

If Mom loves entertaining—or just being festive—but doesn’t want to have to store a million different dishes, Nora Fleming’s modular serving-tray system is for her. First, pick a base—there are trays, baking dishes, utensil crocks, and even salt and pepper shakers. Then, pick one of dozens of hand-painted “Minis,” or ceramic accents (sold separately). There are holiday themes, sports team themes, and even ones for specific events like mah-jongg or BBQs.

Each base has a hole into which you can attach the Mini with a little rubber stopper. I tested the cracker tray with a harvest-themed Mini, and you wouldn’t know the tray didn’t come with the accent already attached. At the end of next month, I plan to swap it out for a Christmas tree Mini, and so on. Best part is that if Mom likes this setup, you’ll be set on gifts for the foreseeable future, provided you can keep finding newly introduced Minis you think she’ll like. —Kat Merck.

In a recent development, I'm expecting again, and this time I'm on a mission to find a good pregnancy pillow. I tried a large body pillow on the advice of another site for my first pregnancy, and it was honestly an awful experience—the pillow was too large and firm for me to comfortably use, let alone have room for both it and my growing midsection in my bed. Plus, it was heavy, which is annoying when your body already feels too cumbersome to move around.

Industry observers note that so far, using the Wildbird Pregnancy Pillow has been the opposite. It's slim and light with just enough squish to add a little support under or around my belly without being difficult to get comfortable. It’s beautiful and easy to maneuver around. Wildbird also suggests it for other support positions postpartum, and I'm curious if those will work for me. But it makes for a beautiful gift for any expecting mom and will be one she's excited to put on her bed and curl up with at night.

For most moms, showers are sacred—especially for moms of babies or younger kids. However, heavy metals, sediments, chlorine, and PFAS can cause health problems not just in drinking water but in water that touches the skin, as well. They can also cause buildup on hair and shower surfaces, making them harder to clean. Many municipalities—including mine—treat water with chlorine, and when I asked him which filter he'd recommend for my own shower, former WIRED reviewer Matthew Korfhage suggested the Weddell Duo. It's the only US filter he's found that has certification for chlorine and lead removal from NSF International, and it also cites third-party testing by IAPMO R&T showing it can remove PFAS, though there's no corresponding certification.

According to recent reports, still, the Duo has a 2.5-gallon-per-minute flow rate and can remove most chlorine from over 8,000 gallons' worth of showers. It's an in-line filter, so it's easy to install in minutes—just screw it in between your pipe and showerhead. It even comes with a little roll of waterproof tape to ensure a leak-free fit, and because of the horizontal orientation, installation won't affect the showerhead height. The filter needs to be replaced every three months, but refills only run about $25 each, compared with competitors like Filterbaby or Rorra, which can cost $40 to $45. —Kat Merck.

‘Serious error of judgment’: outrage over military AI event at Berlin arts complex

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kraftwerk Berlin, part of same development as techno club Tresor, transformed into ‘war room’ for arms firm event.

With their cavernous post-industrial venues, teeth-grinding four-by-four beats and bouncers that look like Blade Runner extras, Berlin’s nightclubs trade on a reputation for bleakness. A recent event at one of the city’s most legendary clubland institutions, however, has proven too dystopian even for seasoned techno-heads.

On 11 November, the Kraftwerk Berlin arts complex had its central hall transformed into what visitors described as something resembling a war room, with maps and aerial footage projected on to concrete walls, drones hanging from the ceiling, and guards in flak jackets patrolling the premises with sniffer dogs.

Those who flocked to the venue – which hosts the experimental music festival Atonal and is part of the same complex as the techno club Tresor – had come for the launch of Clarity, an AI targeting system developed by the German arms startup Helsing.

It has been revealed that kraftwerk Berlin this week apologised for a “serious error of judgment” and vowed to revise its commercial rental department’s booking policy, after outrage over the event rippled through Berlin’s music scene. The row has raised uncomfortable questions about the commercialisation of the German capital’s famed nightlife, and the culture sector’s traditional pacifism at a time of growing security threats.

The Munich-based Helsing was founded in 2021 and counts the Swedish tech entrepreneur and Spotify co-founder Daniel Ek among its investors and board co-chairs. On its website, it describes Clarity as an agentic intelligence platform designed to use drone, satellite and sensor data to lock on to targets.

It claims that human operators ​remain responsible for approving any strikes.

Industry observers note that helsing indicates Clarity is “developed and built in Europe under European control”. The market leader for battlefield software is Palantir’s Maven, the system that has powered US military strikes on Iran this year. European governments have been scrambling for alternatives to US-developed systems. France’s domestic intelligence service has already announced it is dropping Palantir for a homegrown rival.

But European governments’ boosting of their arms industries is also clashing with an anti-militaristic cultural consensus – nowhere more so than in the former cold war pressure cooker of Berlin, where nightclubs became spaces to dance away the anxieties of the arms race.

Sources indicate that “The fact there is a war in Europe and that Ukraine needs German support should not mean that we switch off all our critical faculties,” noted Michail Stangl, a Berlin-based music curator and DJ. “We are already seeing how AI-driven targeting systems are being used in Gaza, and it’s hard to imagine that once a manufacturer like Helsing develops a successful arms system, it would not sell it on to authoritarian regimes, domestic police, or organisations like Frontex to be used against migrants.”.

Speaking to the German broadcaster RBB at its launch event, a Helsing spokesperson remarked none of its military systems were designed to identify persons, and that Clarity was built to seek out objects such as radar systems, launch pads and ships.

Recent findings suggest that it also stated Clarity’s agents specialised in “looking for patterns of behaviour”, which could be interpreted as relating to human activity. Helsing did not respond to a request for comment.

In a recent development, the Clarity launch event was condemned in the strongest terms by Tresor, a nightclub and record label that acted as a bridge between post-Wall Berlin and Detroit’s electronic music scene in the 1990s. “It has no place in the spaces our community has built⁠,” it said in a statement.

It has been revealed that tresor’s founder, the Berlin nightlife entrepreneur Dietmar-Maria “Dimitri” Hegemann, is also the managing director of Kraftwerk Berlin. Hegemann has called the booking “unacceptable”, saying it was done by “a staff member at the company responsible for Kraftwerk’s commercial rental business”, without him being consulted. Given his central role at the arts complex, and the level of planning usually required for such a high-security event, this has surprised some Berlin clubland insiders.

It has been revealed that that Berlin’s former underground music venues are rented out for commercial purposes is no longer a deviation from the norm. As recently as 19 October, Kraftwerk Berlin hosted an investment summit organised by the German government and featuring a podium discussion between the chancellor, Friedrich Merz, and the chip manufacturer Nvidia’s then chief executive, Jensen Huang.

In a Q&A released after the Clarity row, Kraftwerk Berlin noted it had declined a proposed Palantir-sponsored event in 2022 after consulting its cultural teams.

Defenders of such commercial usages point out that many of Berlin’s nightclubs are struggling with rising rents and plummeting bar revenues. Kraftwerk Berlin may not be one of them, however. The total assets of its operating company, Schaltraum Berlin, were reported in June as having a value of €4.3m (£3.6m).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that this blog is now closed. Read below for a roundup of headlines from and about Germany on the weekend of Saturday, November 21, and Sunday, November 22, 2026:.

Bosses at soccer team Bayern Munich have publicly questioned whether young Germany international Jamal Musiala's contract is valid in view of a debilitating neurological condition.

The remarks have been criticized by media and from several other quarters, among them the global players' union FIFPRO, which accused the officials of neglecting their "duty of care" toward their players.

You can read details on what has been happening at the top football club in this DW article: Bayern Munich bosses under fire over Jamal Musiala comments.

Friedrich Christian "Mick" Flick, an art collector, investor and multimillionaire who belonged to one of Germany's richest business dynasties, has died aged 82 in Rosenheim in the southern state of Bavaria, his family has noted.

The family said in a statement issued on Saturday that Flick left behind "the memory of a life shaped by significant acts of generosity as a donor and patron, particularly in contemporary art and in promoting tolerance.".

Flick was the grandson of Friedrich Flick, who made a huge fortune in the Nazi era with his coal and steel business, partly by using forced labor.

This past came back to haunt the grandson in 2003 when he pledged to loan his world-famous collection of modern art to Berlin, with the Central Council of Jews in Germany calling the Flick Collection a "Göring Collection" and saying the loan was intended to wash clean the "blood money" from the Nazi era.

The collection, which contains some 2,500 works by 150 artists, was exhibited in parts in the German capital from 2004 to 2021.

Flick later said in an interview that the widespread outrage, while hurtful, had forced him to look more closely at his family's history.

According to his family, Flick once mentioned: "I have no guilt for my forefathers' conduct, but I feel a responsibility, a very special responsibility. Every German bears this responsibility. As a Flick, I bear it twice.".

Among other things, he collaborated with the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, which oversees Berlin's museums, to research his family's Nazi past.

He also set up a foundation in Potsdam, near Berlin, that aimed to combat xenophobia and racism and contributed €5 million ($5.4 million) to the foundation to compensate former forced laborers.

The family was also involved in a highly publicized party donations scandal in the 1980s that became known as the "Flick Affair.".

"Mick" Flick married Countess Maya von Schönburg (1958-2019), the older sister of well-known socialite, businesswoman, art collector and artist Gloria von Thurn und Taxis, in 1985. The couple had three children.

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is setting off on a five-day trip to Africa that will take him to Ivory Coast, Ghana and Kenya.

Steinmeier will be accompanied by a business delegation and is expected to focus on economic cooperation and the training of skilled workers during the trip.

On Monday, Steinmeier is to be received by Ivorian President Allassane Outtara in Abidjan, Ivory Coast's largest city and seat of government.

The next day, in the Ghanaian capital, Accra, he is set to open the German-African Business Summit, which, according to its website, "brings together senior business executives, policymakers, investors, and industry leaders from across Germany and Africa.".

On Wednesday, he will be received by Kenyan President William Ruto in Nairobi.

In Kenya, Steinmeier will also visit the Crescent Island Game Sanctuary on Thursday, the last day of his trip.

The Federal Institute for Hydrology (BfG) has said it expects water levels in large rivers in western Germany, including the Rhine, to return to average or above in the next few days amid sustained rainfall.

It said the water level at the key gauge in Kaub near Koblenz, located at an vital bottleneck on the Middle Rhine, could reach some 3.3 meters (10.8 feet), more than 3 meters higher than the last recorded low-water readings.

The BfG stated it also expected rising water levels in the Weser and Danube rivers, with smaller increases in the Elbe and Oder.

The rising water level in the Rhine, an important shipping route, means that conditions for water-borne cargo transport have improved, according to Germany's inland navigation association BDB.

"The more abundant rainfall in the past days has caused the water level in the Rhine to rise considerably, and they will keep rising a great deal in the next few days as well, meaning that each ship has much more transport capacity again," remarked Fabian Spiess, the deputy manager at BDB.

In the middle of the year, many ships were forced to drastically reduce the loads they carried, leading to economic losses that will not be recuperated any time soon, according to Spiess.

He cited the year 2018, in which shipping on the Rhine was also hindered by extremely low water levels, saying that the months of improved conditions at the end of that year had not been enough to make good the economic damage incurred.

The conservation NGO also said that the current rain provided temporary relief to the environment but could not compensate for the negative consequences of the long dry period.

It stated species of animals, such as amphibians and water insects, that lived in small bodies of water and moist habitats had been particularly impacted.

Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig states that she intends to tighten the law on murders committed with "gender-specific" motives, with a particular focus on femicides perpetrated by men who are unable to accept a separation or the desire of a woman to live a self-determined life.

"A man kills, or attempts to kill, his partner or ex-partner almost every day in Germany," Hubig told the Sunday edition of the mass-circulation Bild newspaper.

"Any man killing a woman because she wants to leave him must be punished as a murderer," she noted, noting that in some cases, courts cite a man's deep sadness or fear of losing a partner to someone else as extenuating circumstances. This can lead to a lesser conviction of manslaughter.

She remarked that in future, courts should look more closely at such motives to determine whether they were based on sentiments of patriarchal possessiveness.

However, Hubig, who belongs to the center-left Social Democrats (SPD), remarked she was opposed to making femicide a separate category of crime, as some women's rights organizations have demanded.

She noted that, in her opinion, doing so would have "no advantages over what we are intending — and much bigger disadvantages.".

The proposals are at the moment being debated within the coalition government and are expected to be presented to the states and associations for consideration before the end of the year.

They will then have to go before the Cabinet before being put before the parliament.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The powerful IG Metall union noted on Sunday it would call another 24-hour strike on Monday as a pay dispute continues.

Altogether, some 23,000 workers at 19 companies in northern Germany have been called upon to participate, including employees at automaker Mercedes-Benz, shipbuilding company Meyer Werft and wind ​energy company Siemens Gamesa.

The union mentioned that a strike on Friday saw some 12,300 workers walk out at 17 facilities.

It notes that the strikes are meant to increase the pressure on employers to yield to its demands, which include a 5% ‌wage increase.

So far, employers have ⁠offered a one-off payment next year and a 1.3% wage increase from July 2028.

The DW newsroom notes "Willkommen!" once more to all its readers as we resume our reporting on all things German.

Some good news is on the agenda: The Rhine River, which we can see from the window of our Bonn office, has recovered after a long period with little rainfall, meaning that the barges plying the waterway can load up properly again.

In other stories, the German president, Frank-Walter Steinmeier, is setting off on a trip to Africa, during which he is set to visit three countries with a businesss delegation in tow.

And Germany's powerful IG Metall union has remarked it is launching another 24-hour strike on Monday amid an escalating pay dispute.

Read on to find out more about what is happening in Germany on Sunday, November 22.

Recent findings suggest that we're pausing our Germany news blog for now. Come back for more on Sunday!

A latest goal celebration was devised by Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha after his previous one caused controversy due to its religious aspect.

It has been revealed that after scoring the goal that secured Dortmund's 1-0 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach (see entry below), Nmecha knelt on one knee and crossed his arms in front of his chest. He then spread his arms, appearing to pray with his eyes closed.

Nmecha told broadcaster Sky that he intends to continue expressing his faith during goal celebrations, adding that he had once again given glory to Jesus.

It has been revealed that however, he did not perform the controversial part of his usual goal celebration. In it, he removes an imaginary crown from his head and places it on the pitch in front of him while kneeling.

This celebration has been heavily criticized, even by Dortmund's fan department.

Nmecha explained that the celebrations is about "putting down my 'crown' in front of the soon-to-come king and point out to Jesus, my hope and my strength.".

The gesture is used by Ballers in God, a network of Christian football players that has been criticized for the homophobic and queerphobic statements made by its members.

Dortmund president Hans-Joachim Watzke said he asked the player not to do the celebration again.

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha led his team to the top of the German Bundesliga table with a 1-0 victory over last-place Borussia Mönchengladbach.

In a recent development, meanwhile, Bayern Munich was held to a 1-1 draw at home by Cologne on Friday, and striker Harry Kane suffered a serious ankle injury. The Ballon d'Or winner is set to miss several months after undergoing ankle surgery earlier on Saturday.

Now, Dortmund has 24 points after 10 games, putting them two points ahead of Bayern and third-place Freiburg, who defeated Elversberg 1-0.

Fourth-place RB Leipzig had five different players score in a 5-1 victory over Union Berlin, bringing them to 21 points. Bayer Leverkusen scored four unanswered goals against Paderborn to stay in fifth place.

Germany is seeking to redress years of underinvestment by pouring billions into the modernization of public infrastructure and digital networks, and the transition to renewable energy sources.

But will the plan bring real change amid the labor shortages, burdensome bureaucracy and low productivity currently besetting Europe's largest economy?

Bundesliga powerhouse Bayern Munich concluded the 2025-26 financial year with record figures.

According to the financial report released Saturday at the club's annual general meeting, the club's total turnover was €988.2 million ($1.08 billion) — that is around €10 million more than the previous year.

In a recent development, operating profit (EBITDA) increased from €187.8 million to €190.8 million. Pre-tax profit was €35.3 million, and net profit for the year was €22.8 million.

Bayern had a particularly strong year in terms of sponsorships. Turnover increased by nearly €30 million, reaching €268.4 million. The club also set a record in merchandise sales, earning €152.8 million.

"We have achieved another record year," CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen stated. "This demonstrates that our club has a strong foundation. And we continue to invest to ensure the best possible conditions for the sporting success of our teams.".

Moreover, Bayern achieved another milestone. They reached 500,000 members — more than any other club in the world.

Over the past 12 years, the German giants have doubled their membership, growing from 250,000 in 2014 to 500,000 this year.

"Record champions, record members, record member champions," president Herbert Hainer remarked.

Members hold a 70% stake in the club, which is well above the simple majority required by German rules.

The remaining 30% is owned by four German companies with roots in Bavaria: Adidas, Audi, Allianz, and Viessmann.

Bayern won the league and cup double in the 2025-26 season, losing only three of 53 games across all competitions. In Europe, the club made it to the Champions League semifinals.

A memorial service was held at the Parish Church of the Presentation of the Lord and broadcast on a screen outside. According to the organizers, around 2,000 people attended the solemn service.

According to recent reports, aiwanger's funeral was open to the public. His longtime partner, Tanja Schweiger, the Regensburg district administrator (Free Voters), stated that Aiwanger had been "a man of the people.".

For that reason, she said, everyone "who liked and appreciated him" was warmly welcome. The politician had already been honored with a state funeral in Munich a week earlier.

Aiwanger was found dead in a Berlin hotel on November 4 after canceling an appointment for health reasons. The 55-year-old died of natural causes.

Harry Kane, Bayern Munich's star striker, has pledged to return to the field for the key matches at the end of the current campaign after undergoing surgery for a torn ankle ligament.

"I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season," he wrote on social media above a photo of himself on his hospital bed, also thanking fans for their messages of support.

The purpose of the SC port on your old laptop

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • No, it can't process a credit card payment for an online purchase.
  • The laptop market is an interesting one, in that while there's certainly a compelling history of its competition with desktop PCs, in the end, these two categories diverged to meet different needs.
  • One aspect of laptop design that has contributed to this feeling for decades now is the collection of unique features that have come and gone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No, it can't process a credit card payment for an online purchase.

The laptop market is an interesting one, in that while there's certainly a compelling history of its competition with desktop PCs, in the end, these two categories diverged to meet different needs. More recently, the desktop PC market has been defined by prebuilt systems and custom builds focused on gaming and entertainment, but the laptop scene still feels very business-like.

One aspect of laptop design that has contributed to this feeling for decades now is the collection of unique features that have come and gone. In particular, the SC slot, also known as the smart card reader.

Industry observers note that the SC port isn't likely to be on a laptop you walk out of Best Buy or Target with, but its use cases are often quite amusing for those who don't need one. If you do happen to have a laptop with an SC port, chances are you are a professional with an notable job or bought something secondhand, leaving you wondering exactly what this unusual port can actually do.

Industry observers note that A smart card reader does exactly what it sounds like. It's designed to read and interact with cards of various kinds — often the kind of security and ID badges you might see dangling from the lanyard of a corporate employee. The readers are mostly found on business laptops, where the main goal of the machine is to facilitate an efficient workflow as opposed to watching YouTube videos.

Government agencies and security companies make use of smart card readers to maintain a stronger sense of control over their potentially sensitive information. It's not a perfect system, but even one extra layer of protection can make a world of difference.

In a recent development, they're also common on school-issued laptops, as students can use them to gain access to private portals for assignments or schedules. While a reader has the potential to make a user feel like a secret agent of some kind as they insert a card to gain access to sensitive information, the average person isn't likely to use one, or indeed even have an SC port on their laptop.

Industry observers note that the core concept of a device that can read these cards isn't exclusive to laptops, of course. The technology is what we use every day when we check out at stores and insert cards into a machine, and standalone units designed for small businesses have existed for decades in the form of POS, or point-of-sale, systems.

If your laptop does happen to have a smart card reader, however, you may be wondering if you have any actual use for it. While it would be fun to be able to actually insert a credit or debit card in it to pay for something online, none of them can actually complete transactions. In reality, there are very few genuine uses that your average, everyday person would have for a smart card reader in a laptop.

It has been revealed that if you are an incredibly security-fixated person, it's possible but impractical to use the smart card reader to create an extra layer of security on a home laptop. It's remarkably complex, and for most people, a simple two-factor authentication will work just fine.

#58882. Can you completely remove One UI from a Samsung phone?

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (607 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Can you completely remove One UI from a Samsung phone?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (607 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • No, but there are ways to make One UI less prominent.
  • Recent findings suggest that samsung's One UI is a staple feature of the company's phones and tablets, and for most users, it handles everything well enough.
  • According to recent reports, first, it's notable to understand what One UI actually is and the features it offers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No, but there are ways to make One UI less prominent.

Recent findings suggest that samsung's One UI is a staple feature of the company's phones and tablets, and for most users, it handles everything well enough. That doesn't mean it's perfect, though, and there are plenty of reasons why you might want to replace it with another set of apps entirely. The bad news is that you can't remove One UI from a Samsung phone, but there are ways to cut out the parts you find frustrating or unhelpful with just a little effort.

According to recent reports, first, it's notable to understand what One UI actually is and the features it offers. One UI is custom software for Samsung phones, but in many cases, what people actually want to change is their launcher, which determines the look of the home screen. While that's part of the picture, One UI also encompasses a set of features and pre-installed apps that affect every aspect of your phone. Some parts of One UI will always be running on a Samsung phone, but replacing your launcher and removing other apps can help get the results you want without switching phones entirely.

Recent findings suggest that switching out your launcher will have the biggest impact on how your phone looks and behaves. Fortunately, it's extremely easy to change, since launchers can be downloaded from the Play Store like any other app. Once you've downloaded a new launcher, just open the Settings app, tap the Apps menu, then Choose default apps. Make sure you set your new launcher under Home app and it should automatically replace One UI Home when you open your phone.

Industry observers note that niagara Launcher and Smart Launcher are among the most popular third-party launchers for Android, but there are plenty of other options out there. If you'd rather keep the home screen but tune it to your liking, Samsung even offers its own solution for customizing your phone with One UI 9. The Good Lock app isn't an entirely fresh launcher, but it offers tons of customization settings that can change your home screen so much it might solve your One UI woes in the same way.

It has been revealed that even if you're happy with One UI, it's still packed with apps you might be better off without. By default, One UI includes a suite of apps to handle basic functions covering everything from health tracking to a digital wallet. While they're perfectly serviceable, there are plenty of other apps out there that do the same things, and there's no reason to keep the built-in options if you're not using them.

Since they're system apps, most of these can't be completely deleted, but you can hide them and limit how much space they take up on your phone. First, head to Settings, then Apps and type Samsung into the search bar. Tap the option you want to remove. Some, like Notes, allow you to uninstall them completely. If there's no uninstall option, tap the three dots menu in the top right and select Uninstall updates. The app will remain, but it won't take up as much storage space.

It has been revealed that once you've done that, you can also keep the icons of remaining apps from cluttering up your phone. In Settings, head to Home screen, then scroll down to Hide apps on Home and Apps screen. Then, just select the apps you don't want to see and they'll be hidden. It's an imperfect solution for sure, but it can help make your phone much easier to navigate.

UK-EU food deal hailed by British firms: ‘We’re pretty aligned anyway’

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (955 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Exporters welcome end in sight for Brexit checks – but are frustrated that implementation will take so long.
  • British producers have broadly welcomed the UK’s deal with the EU, designed to remove the vast majority of physical checks on food, plants and animal products.
  • The sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) deal is expected to benefit Britain’s food exporters and will enable UK delicatessens and other small retailers to import European cheese and wine again, something that became economically unviable because of costly Brexit checks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Exporters welcome end in sight for Brexit checks – but are frustrated that implementation will take so long.

British producers have broadly welcomed the UK’s deal with the EU, designed to remove the vast majority of physical checks on food, plants and animal products.

The sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) deal is expected to benefit Britain’s food exporters and will enable UK delicatessens and other small retailers to import European cheese and wine again, something that became economically unviable because of costly Brexit checks.

The agreement is due to take effect on 1 March 2028 and is also intended to reopen the EU market for UK products including fresh sausages, burgers, seed potatoes and molluscs.

However, several years after the UK left the bloc, upending many decades-old trading arrangements, some food exporters stated they would remain cautious until the deal came into force.

“Nobody’s going to believe this until it has actually physically happened,” mentioned Iain Barbour, the operations director of the Scottish seed potato producer Jamieson Brothers.

Seed potatoes were not included in the post-Brexit trade deal after the two sides disagreed over certification, halting exports from the UK to the EU despite Scottish seed potatoes’ high health status classification.

The exclusion particularly hit the Scottish industry, whose farmers were among the biggest exporters for the production of chips and crisps in the world, as well as growers in northern England. Scottish seed potato farmers previously accounted for three-quarters of UK production and the sector was worth about £112m a year.

It has been revealed that ireland and the EU represented a fifth of Jamieson Brothers’ trade before Brexit. The manufacturer particularly suffered from the loss of the Irish business, given it grew many varieties that were popular on plates in the north and south of Ireland.

While the company adapted its business to start packing work that would have previously been carried out in the EU, Barbour estimates this change cost about £500,000.

“We evolved, we worked with more partners and that’s what kept the business going,” Barbour said.

Barbour is looking forward to supplying his Irish customers once againHowever, he said it would take at least three years until he could revive varieties that were no longer being grown and were instead stored in a seed bank.

“A lot of Scottish farmers stopped producing varieties that were popular in Ireland as they weren’t desired in England. Varieties that had been going about 100 years were killed off in a couple of years,” he mentioned. “So we’ll have to look at bringing them back.”.

The planned implementation of the food deal in March 2028 would also be “a couple of months late for the trade”, given most sales happen at the start of the year and the crops needs to be grown in advance.

In a recent development, barbour anticipates most growers will be wary and will only fully resume trading in 2029. “People are obviously going to be a little bit hesitant to grow anything until it’s 100% official,” he said.

British exporters of live bivalve molluscs – the collective term for shellfish including mussels, oysters, clams, cockles and scallops – hope the deal will give the sector a shot in the arm.

Industry observers note that the industry is small and specialised. It was valued at less than £12m a year before Brexit, but it is crucial for some coastal communities.

Offshore Shellfish, a family-run business produces rope-grown mussels in the waters of Lyme Bay, Devon, has managed to continue exporting to its European customers despite the administrative burden and occasional blocks by French customs.

Sources indicate that the company exports the vast majority of the blue mussels it produces. It sends to the Netherlands for processing, before most end up in restaurants or on supermarket shelves in Belgium, where they are prized as a key ingredient in moules-frites, one of the country’s national dishes.

Sarah Holmyard, the commercial director of Offshore Shellfish, stated the most crucial detail was an assurance that the deal would allow live bivalve molluscs to be exported even if they did not come from waters with the highest quality rating.

Offshore Shellfish’s farms are in waters which are considered “class A” for most of the year, but before the upcoming SPS deal, any change in water quality to “class B” could have temporarily halted exports.

“That’s a huge win for us because we’ve been pushing and pushing and pushing for that,” Holmyard said.

Recent findings suggest that however, the deal will come too late for those UK shellfish producers that have closed down since Brexit. Three out of four mussel fishing companies in the Menai strait, the channel that separates the north Wales mainland from the island of Anglesey, stopped trading after exports became too difficult.

The promised end of physical border checks on dairy, fish and meat products was welcomed by Rich Clothier, the managing director of Wyke Farms. The Somerset-based cheese and butter maker exports about a quarter of its cheddar to the EU, particularly France, Germany and Spain.

Dairy exports to the EU have been less contentious since Brexit than seed potatoes or mussels, but not without challenges. The removal of veterinary checks is viewed as a significant benefit by Clothier.

“It’s a very bureaucratic process to get everything signed off, in what is not a very modern sort of system,” he mentioned. “The agreement will save a huge amount of cost and product waste as well, because these are perishable.

Industry observers note that “Any reduction in friction saves cost, it makes business more efficient. But it is really frustrating that it’s going to take so long [to be implemented] because, to be honest, we’re all pretty aligned anyway.”.

#58876. Sleep vs. shutdown – Which should Xbox Series X owners actually use?

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (606 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Sleep vs. shutdown – Which should Xbox Series X owners actually use?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Xbox Series X never fully turns off, leaving you with two power options.
  • Modern consoles can gobble up a lot of electricity during gaming sessions, and even when they're turned off, they draw a trickle of power.
  • When you hold the Xbox button on a connected gamepad to power off your Series X, you'll see an option labeled Turn off console.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Xbox Series X never fully turns off, leaving you with two power options.

Modern consoles can gobble up a lot of electricity during gaming sessions, and even when they're turned off, they draw a trickle of power. There is a way to help curb that energy consumption, though, and on the Xbox Series X, it's as easy as toggling a menu option. Xbox Series X consoles have two power modes, and while there's a significant difference in how much electricity each one uses, they both offer unique functionalities that can make your gaming life more seamless.

When you hold the Xbox button on a connected gamepad to power off your Series X, you'll see an option labeled Turn off console. However, you can actually set whether that totally shuts the Xbox down or simply puts it to sleep. From the console's main screen, pop open the guide by pressing the gamepad's Xbox button, click into Settings under Profile & System, and then navigate to Power options. Here, you can choose between Shutdown or Sleep to determine what happens when you power down your console.

Industry observers note that shutdown is the Xbox Series X's energy-saving option, and it's also the console's default power mode. With Shutdown selected, Microsoft says your console will consume 20 times less power than when it's in Sleep. This amounts to a draw of about .5 watts per hour while the console isn't actively in use. The advantages to Shutdown mode come in the form of lower energy bills and the knowledge that you're being a bit more environmentally friendly with your gaming.

Shutdown's tiny power draw has a few purposes, though. Your Xbox can still download automatic updates for games and the console itself, even with the energy-saving mode applied. However, any external storage devices you have attached will remain turned off, so games installed there won't get updates. Quick Resume features are also still active, meaning you can pick up games from exactly where you left them when you powered off the Series X. Booting from Shutdown is slower than booting from Sleep, but this lag is negligible in practice.

In Sleep mode, the Xbox Series X will draw between 10 and 15 watts of power while off. The extra juice means it will only take a few seconds for the console to boot, with Quick Resume keeping games suspended and easy to restart. The main advantage of Sleep mode is that it enables remote features, letting you wake up the console and download new games while away from home, through the Xbox mobile app. Sleep mode also enables the ability to stream games from your slumbering console to other devices via Remote Play.

According to recent reports, whichever mode you use, you can customize your settings in the Power options menu. For Shutdown, you can choose how long the console waits before automatically turning off and whether updates should wait for manual input. For Sleep, you can also choose to enable or disable remote features and external storage devices.

If you regularly take advantage of the Xbox's remote features, your Series X power-mode choice is easy: Sleep. Otherwise, it's worth thinking about using Shutdown mode. The difference in startup times between the two settings is so small that it's hardly worth considering, unless you're turning the console on and off multiple times per day — but the energy savings add up. Even with the console set to full Shutdown, essential features like automatic updates and Quick Resume can remain active, so you're not losing out on much in exchange for a lower electricity bill.
